# Lesson 2 Solutions to the E-Waste Problem

**The 3 R’s:  Reducing, Reusing, Recycling**

Which R is most important, and why?  And why is it the hardest to do?

| Reducing \-  reusing and recycling are band-aids to the problem, they don’t solve it. People like shiny toys, the latest and greatest. Also helps make your life easiest |
| :---- |

**Recycling**

[Here’s a video on the modern state of recycling in Ontario.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ARBqPuvYq0c)

So we all recycle paper and plastic regularly (with questionable success), but why do so few people recycle electronics?

Let’s watch [this video on how e-waste is recycled](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zU62hh3DBfg) to get an idea why.

The good news:  

| Some countries do have the facilities/recourse to recycle some electronics and other waste |
| :---- |

The bad news: 

| Most electronic components are not valuable enough to for companies/governments to recycle. |
| :---- |

So if recycling isn’t the solution, what about reuse?

**Device Repair (Reuse/Reduce)**

Why do so few people buy used phones or get their phones repaired?

On your own, check out this video on [Laptop Repair](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d_H054zwCOY). (\~6 min)![][image1]  
*WARNING:* This guy is pretty eccentric  
   
Then, we will watch this one together: [iPhone Repair](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rCUMMDXJMuk)

Moral of the story:  
Electronics can be repaired\!  So if your phone stops working, or the screen cracks, or your game console breaks, make an effort to repair it instead of just throwing it out to buy a new one.

**E-waste Solutions**

We’ve discussed some of the problems involving e-waste. What are some solutions? Group up and brainstorm a few. Focus on the **Reduce** and **Reuse** parts of the equation, as we’ve seen Recycling can only get us so far. Ideas may include:

- Regulations  
- Education Programs  
- Incentives (for individuals or businesses)


| Don’t use it Promote a circular economy through repairing, refurbishing, and recycling, Make "right to repair" legislation, makke sure to enforce extended producer responsibility, and designing more durable electronics.  |
